tier.reason: Scripts: 1 Python script and 3 command scripts

headline: 1 thing blocks this on macOS and 5 need a fix.

aiUsage.reason: Some fixes need judgement (a library swap, a different API), so expect some AI use.

findings.title: Uses a module that only exists on Windows
findings.why: winreg only exists on Windows; on a Mac the import fails.
findings.fixPattern: Import it only on Windows (if sys.platform == "win32":) and use a settings file (json, plistlib) or the platformdirs package on a Mac.

findings.title: Script has Windows line endings
findings.why: A Mac reads the extra carriage return at the end of each line as part of the command, so the script fails with "command not found" or "bad interpreter".
findings.fixPattern: Convert to LF line endings, and add `*.sh text eol=lf` to .gitattributes so they stay that way.

findings.title: Uses a path that only exists on this computer
findings.why: C:\Users\sam\Documents\Bank exports is a folder on the computer this was written on; it won't exist on macOS.
findings.fixPattern: Build the path from the project folder or the user's home instead: Path(__file__).parent / "data", Path.home(), or path.join(__dirname, "data") in Node.

findings.title: Builds paths with backslashes
findings.evidence: with open(EXPORTS + "\\" + month + ".csv", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
findings.why: Backslashes only separate folders on Windows; on a Mac they become part of the file name.
findings.fixPattern: Join paths with pathlib (Path(base) / name) or os.path.join; in Node, path.join.

findings.title: Run script has no Mac version
findings.fixPattern: Add a shell script version next to it (start.sh), or replace it with a Python or Node script that runs on both.

findings.title: Calls a function that only exists on Windows
findings.why: os.startfile only exists on Windows, so this line fails on a Mac.
findings.fixPattern: Open files with subprocess.run(["open", path]) on a Mac, behind a platform check.

findings.title: Package builds for macOS weren't checked
findings.why: Some Python packages ship no ready-made build for every OS and have to be compiled. Checking means asking PyPI, and this scan stayed offline.
findings.fixPattern: Scan again with the online package check, or watch for compile errors when installing on macOS.

notes: Nothing in the project was run: no code, scripts, notebooks or package managers.
